title: Add a Remember me checkbox to the sign-in form

test_data.valid_customer: An active portal customer account with valid credentials.
test_data.session_cookie: The portal session cookie identified from the sign-in response or browser cookie store; its name is not specified by the requirement.
test_data.time_reference: Record the current date/time immediately before or at cookie issuance using the agreed test-environment clock.

requirements.text: The sign-in form displays a Remember me checkbox to the left of the Sign in button, unchecked by default.
When the customer signs in with the box checked, the session cookie expiry is set to 30 days from the current date/time.
When the customer signs in with the box unchecked, the existing session-cookie behaviour is preserved (expires on browser close).
The checkbox state is not remembered between visits (always renders unchecked on page load).
Cookie must carry Secure and HttpOnly flags.
No change to the underlying identity-provider handshake.

test_cases.title: Display Remember me to the left of Sign in and leave it unchecked by default
preconditions: The sign-in form is available in a test environment.
No previously rendered page is relied upon.
steps: Open the sign-in page.
Locate the Remember me checkbox and the Sign in button.
Compare their displayed positions.
Inspect the initial selection state of the checkbox.
expected_results: A checkbox labelled Remember me is displayed.
The Remember me checkbox is positioned to the left of the Sign in button.
The checkbox is unchecked when the sign-in page initially renders.

test_cases.title: Issue a 30-day session cookie when Remember me is selected
preconditions: A valid customer account is available.
Cookie attributes can be inspected in the sign-in response or browser cookie store.
The test-environment current date/time can be recorded.
steps: Open the sign-in page.
Select Remember me.
Record the current date/time immediately before submitting valid credentials.
Submit the sign-in form.
Identify the issued portal session cookie and inspect its expiry value.
Calculate the interval from the recorded issuance time to the cookie expiry.
expected_results: The selected sign-in completes according to the existing sign-in outcome.
The issued portal session cookie has an expiry set to 30 days from the current date/time.
The observed expiry is assessed at the 30-day boundary using the agreed clock precision; no alternate duration is accepted.

test_cases.title: Preserve browser-session cookie behaviour when Remember me is unselected
preconditions: A valid customer account is available.
Cookie attributes can be inspected in the sign-in response or browser cookie store.
steps: Open the sign-in page.
Leave Remember me unselected.
Submit valid customer credentials.
Identify and inspect the issued portal session cookie.
Close the browser session.
Start a new browser session and visit the portal.
expected_results: The issued portal session cookie retains browser-session behaviour and has no persistent expiry applicable beyond browser close.
After the browser session is closed, the portal session is no longer available in the new browser session.

test_cases.title: Reset Remember me to unchecked on a subsequent sign-in-page visit
preconditions: A valid customer account is available for the selected-sign-in path.
steps: Open the sign-in page and select Remember me.
Sign in with valid credentials.
Return to the sign-in page in a subsequent visit by ending the authenticated journey or using an available sign-out path.
Inspect the Remember me checkbox when the page loads.
Refresh the sign-in page and inspect the checkbox again.
expected_results: The Remember me checkbox renders unchecked on the subsequent sign-in-page load despite prior selection.
The Remember me checkbox renders unchecked after the page refresh.

test_cases.title: Apply Secure and HttpOnly to the persistent session cookie
preconditions: A valid customer account is available.
The sign-in response or browser developer tooling exposes session-cookie attributes.
steps: Open the sign-in page.
Select Remember me and submit valid credentials.
Identify the issued portal session cookie.
Inspect its Secure and HttpOnly attributes.
expected_results: The session cookie issued for the selected Remember me path carries the Secure flag.
The same session cookie carries the HttpOnly flag.

test_cases.title: Apply Secure and HttpOnly to the browser-session cookie
preconditions: A valid customer account is available.
The sign-in response or browser developer tooling exposes session-cookie attributes.
steps: Open the sign-in page.
Leave Remember me unselected and submit valid credentials.
Identify the issued portal session cookie.
Inspect its Secure and HttpOnly attributes.
expected_results: The session cookie issued for the unselected Remember me path carries the Secure flag.
The same session cookie carries the HttpOnly flag.
This path remains a browser-session cookie as specified in AC-3.

test_cases.title: Verify the identity-provider handshake is unchanged for both Remember me selections
preconditions: A baseline capture or approved observable definition of the pre-change identity-provider handshake is available.
A valid customer account is available.
Network or identity-provider observability is available for both sign-in attempts.
steps: Capture or obtain the approved baseline identity-provider handshake for a portal sign-in.
Sign in with Remember me selected and capture the identity-provider handshake.
Sign in with Remember me unselected and capture the identity-provider handshake.
Compare each captured handshake with the approved baseline using the agreed comparison method.
expected_results: The identity-provider handshake for the selected path is unchanged from the approved baseline.
The identity-provider handshake for the unselected path is unchanged from the approved baseline.
Cookie persistence is assessed separately through AC-2 and AC-3 and is not treated as an identity-provider handshake change.

open_test_execution_dependencies: The session-cookie name and exact cookie-inspection method are not specified.
The time-source precision and permitted measurement tolerance for the 30-day expiry are not specified.
NFR-2 requires an approved baseline capture or observable definition of the existing identity-provider handshake.
